target_customer: People seeking free emotional support in chat, with paid therapy and subscriptions added later
problem: People want to talk to someone without judgment but forums are slow and therapy is costly or stigmatized. 7 Cups connects them anonymously with trained volunteer listeners.
business_model: free volunteer listener chat with paid subscriptions and licensed therapist services; at launch monetization was undecided and listeners could charge fees with a commission
product_category: online emotional support and mental health platform

founders.name: Glen Moriarty
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2013-08-05 calls him a clinical psychologist and father of premature twins; Wikipedia says psychologist who founded it in July 2013.

technical_complexity.rationale: Anonymous matching of users to listeners in chat, ratings and background checks; mostly standard web engineering at founding.

defensibility.rationale: A trained volunteer listener community and ratings data are hard to copy quickly, though the chat product itself is simple.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent identified in 2013 coverage; no source shows anyone copying or buying 7 Cups.

market_need_then: TechCrunch 2013 reported about 1,000 call requests a week within weeks of a soft launch with around 100 listeners, showing demand for support that sits between forums and therapy.

branding.name_origin: From a poem by the 9th century Chinese poet Lu Tong, per Wikipedia and TechCrunch 2013.
branding.domain_note: Uses 7cups.com; a sevencups.com site also appears in searches, relationship not established.

identity.logo: teacup mark implied by name, not described in sources

branding.brand_signature: The tea and listening metaphor from the Lu Tong poem

rebrands.why: Not stated; trademark filings show 7 CUPS of Tea in 2014 and 7 CUPS in 2018.

branding.community_and_virality: Large listener community recruited through groups like NAMI and Active Minds in 2013; independent press (Healthline, BetterHelp review, Duke Chronicle) covers the service.

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive, warm name with a story and steady press coverage, but little evidence the brand itself drove growth.

outcome_analysis: 7 Cups showed strong early demand after its 2013 YC batch, with about 1,000 weekly requests within weeks, and has kept operating for over a decade with a large listener network and paid therapy options. Public funding data is missing, so scale and finances are unknown. A 2025 Mashable report on therapists listed without consent in its directory is the only controversy found.
notes: 7cups.com/about returned 403. Outcome search found only unrelated tea news; a second fetch of Wikipedia found no acquisition or layoffs and one 2025 directory controversy. Funding: CB Insights lists a 2013-08 seed from YC with no amount, and an aggregator page claims an unverified 18M raise with no date or investors; neither recorded as a round. Competitors left empty: TechCrunch 2013 names no rivals, only generic online forums; Talkspace and Koko had no 2013 dated source found. Confidence low because funding and competitors are not sourced.
